clue.text: Some cheer jazzy rag tune

indicators.note: something jazzy is jazzed up and lively, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

parts.note: a rag is slang for a cheap newspaper, and The Sun is a British tabloid

explanation.surface: A little cheer comes from a lively ragtime melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jazzy' scrambles SOME CHEER into HERE COMES. THE SUN is a British tabloid newspaper, and 'rag' is a scornful word for such a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles song written by George Harrison is a well-known example of a tune.

clue.text: Person wittering on about marmalade, perhaps, before English party

indicators.note: the bore and his topic come ahead of the letter for English

parts.note: marmalade is one kind of jam, a fruit preserve
someone who witters on at tedious length is a bore

explanation.surface: A tiresome talker who drones on about breakfast spreads heads off to an English party.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Person wittering on about marmalade' as a JAM BORE, someone who is a bore on the subject of jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large, lively celebration or gathering, so it is a kind of party.

clue.text: Like a close shave, or in need of one

definitions.meaning: a ... moment is frighteningly risky, a narrow escape
someone with a lot of hair or stubble needs a shave

explanation.surface: A near miss, or a man who badly needs a razor.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy is informal for dangerous or nerve-racking, and literally means covered in hair, needing a shave.

clue.text: Pull down pants seldom worn by current husband

indicators.note: the current symbol wears the jumbled letters, so it sits among them
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the word seldom is mangled into a new order

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: A husband's rarely worn underpants get pulled down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear but is the anagram signal: SELDOM becomes DEMOLS, with I put in to give DEMOLIS, then H. In British slang 'pants' means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull down a building is to knock it to the ground, a synonym for destroy completely.

clue.text: Try to bag new sound device that's hard to get

indicators.note: to bag is to capture or enclose, so the attempt holds the letter inside it

parts.note: to have a go is to make a try
a mic, short for microphone, picks up sound

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to grab a new piece of audio kit that's scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard to get' looks like scarce goods, but it means hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomic sayings are cryptic and enigmatic, their meaning difficult to grasp.

clue.text: Big shot in golf by idiot breaking record

indicators.note: the golf letter and the idiot break into the record, splitting it open

parts.note: a diary is a daily record
G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a nit is a silly person

explanation.surface: A powerful player on the golf course, by some fool, breaks the course record.
explanation.definitionFit: A dignitary is a person of high rank or office, an important figure, informally a big shot.

clue.text: Pulse fast on one close to arousal

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A racing heartbeat as someone nears arousal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is a seed of the bean family; 'fast' is the period of fasting, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is an edible seed of a legume, and such seeds are called pulses.

clue.text: Crack in part of lounge? Ring phone number from America

indicators.note: the crack goes inside the fireplace word

parts.note: a hearth is the fireplace floor, part of a sitting room, which the British call a lounge
to crack is to break
O is ring-shaped
TEL is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: Someone spots a crack in a hotel lounge and rings to report it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song, not a figure; in Britain a lounge is a living room.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley's 1956 hit is a famous American song, and a song is often called a number.

clue.text: Name associated with a lot of Allies battling

definitions.text: Name associated with a lot of Allies battling

indicators.note: battling suggests struggle and disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement
most of the word, not all of it, is used, dropping the last letter

explanation.surface: A place name linked forever with Allied troops at war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' takes ALLIE from ALLIES; with NAME the letters are rearranged by 'battling'. The whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian site of the decisive 1942 desert battle is a name tied to the Allied forces fighting.

clue.text: She's housed in dire necessity

indicators.note: the name lives inside the run of letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A woman is living in desperate need.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a woman's name, so it can stand for a female person, she.

clue.text: Ban poetic entreaty to hold the writer back

indicators.note: the whole plea is read from end to start

parts.note: O is the poetic exclamation used in addresses and pleas
to grab is to seize and hold
the writer refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A poet's plea for an embrace is outlawed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses O GRAB ME, a lover's poetic plea.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade with another country.

clue.text: Lizard's egg laid in uncultivated land

indicators.note: the egg is laid inside the stretch of wild land

parts.note: a moor is open, untilled upland
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: A reptile lays its egg out on wild heathland.
explanation.definitionFit: Monitors are large tropical lizards of the genus Varanus, including the Komodo dragon.

clue.text: Pods round ship heading west

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means running right to left, so the vessel is reversed

parts.note: Noah's ark is a ship

explanation.surface: Seed pods surround a vessel sailing west.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a vegetable eaten as its long green seed pods, also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: Political coterie or cult? Back it to reform

indicators.note: reforming a group reshapes it, so the letters are re-formed in a new order

explanation.surface: Is a political inner circle really a cult? Support it to change it.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'to reform', which in the surface reads like political reform.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kit-Cat Club was an early 18th-century London club of Whig politicians and writers, a political circle.

clue.text: Several lines as standard on a chart

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a graph is a chart of data

explanation.surface: A few lines are written as standard on a diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a passage of writing, usually running over several lines.

clue.text: Rot back in coarse types of wood

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: yew and ash are two kinds of timber tree

explanation.surface: Decay sets in among some rough sorts of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' looks like decay in wood, but here it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for nonsense or humbug, as is rot, both meaning foolish talk.

clue.text: Red vehicle by pit

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a coal mine is a pit

explanation.surface: A red car is parked by a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a vivid crimson shade, a type of red pigment made from cochineal.

clue.text: Trickster to perform trickery on a person in court

parts.note: to con someone is to swindle them
a juror sits in court to hear a trial

explanation.surface: A con artist tries to deceive someone in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror is a stage magician who performs tricks, so a trickster.

clue.text: Old Dalmatian in bad rain barking around yard

indicators.note: the earlier letters go round the yard letter, enclosing it

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the word rain is scrambled

explanation.surface: An elderly spotted dog barks in the miserable rain, out in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dalmatian' suggests the dog, but Dalmatia is a coast on the Adriatic; 'barking' turns RAIN into RIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Illyrians were an ancient people of the Balkan coast, including Dalmatia, so an Illyrian was an old Dalmatian.

clue.text: What could make apt stage entertainment

parts.note: the letters of the word tap, set dancing, could give the word apt

explanation.surface: A question about what makes a fitting show.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, means scramble TAP, which can give APT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap dancing, with metal-plated shoes beating rhythms, is a popular theatrical act.

clue.text: This stimulates philosopher

definitions.meaning: a slang name for a small vial of nitrite inhaled for a rush
Karl ... was an Austrian-British philosopher of science

explanation.surface: A thinker who gets the mind racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The inhaled drug gives a brief stimulant rush, and Karl Popper was a famous philosopher.

clue.text: King of music in racy novel that's short

indicators.note: the bluesman goes inside the jumbled letters
novel means new, so the letters of racy appear in a new order

parts.note: B.B. King was the famous American blues guitarist

explanation.surface: A musical monarch appears in a short, saucy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book in the surface but signals the anagram, giving CRAY; 'King of music' is the blues guitarist B.B. King, not a royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short with someone means being curt and irritable, as a crabby person is.

clue.text: Stick crumbling, the end falling off

indicators.note: the final letter drops away from the word

parts.note: flaky means crumbling into ...

explanation.surface: A walking stick crumbles until its tip snaps off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' is not a rod but criticism, as in giving someone stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak and stick both mean harsh criticism or abuse, as in taking flak.

clue.text: Reptile steps out of line

indicators.note: the letter for line is taken out of the steps

parts.note: a ladder is a set of steps

explanation.surface: A snake moves out of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steps out of line' reads as misbehaving, but it is LADDER without L.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is a venomous European snake, a kind of reptile.

clue.text: Parking in great city around shops

indicators.note: the parking letter sits inside the turned letters
turned around means read backwards

parts.note: A1, written AI, means excellent or great
Rome is the Italian capital
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Car parks in a big city surround the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great' is A1, written with the letter I standing for the digit; 'around' reverses it with the city to give EMORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia, the plural of emporium, are large stores or trading places.

clue.text: Don't cook enough food, red nuts having been shelled and sent back

indicators.note: the inner run is then read from end to start
shelling strips away the outer parts, so only an inner run of the letters remains

explanation.surface: An undercooked meal, with red nuts shelled and returned to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been shelled' leaves ODREDNU from the middle of the three words, which 'sent back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To underdo food is to cook it too little, leaving it underdone or rare.

clue.text: Go through group of countries, probing distinctive feature

indicators.note: something probing pushes inside, so the bloc goes within the feature

parts.note: USP stands for unique selling point, a product's distinctive feature
the EU, European Union, is a group of countries

explanation.surface: A union of nations investigates what sets something apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through supplies is to exhaust or consume them entirely.

clue.text: Type of firm with no money to lose it

parts.note: broke means penniless
to lose it is to fly into a rage

explanation.surface: A penniless company goes and loses its temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A brokerage is a business acting as an agent for clients buying and selling, a kind of company.
